verdicts.verdict: Recommend acceptance after minor-to-moderate revision. The statistical substance holds up under direct audit: every estimate I traced reproduces from results/primary2_*.csv in a single rounding step, including the derived quantities most exposed to double rounding (the 0.071/0.066 to 0.058/0.051 age-restriction gaps, the 0.015/0.018/0.012 parsimony losses, the 28%/50% food-insecurity shares, the four fairness flag deltas, and the 0.0002/0.0044 five-versus-six margin). All confidence intervals bracket their estimates with plausible widths for 728 and 661 events, and the between-cycle interval (-0.045 to +0.056) is exactly what the two cohort intervals imply for a difference of independent samples, which is a real internal-consistency check passed. The rescaled cluster bootstrap is documented to reproduction standard in Part D, singleton-stratum pooling and domain-estimate construction included, and validated against a linearized design-based standard error. The oracle is correctly labeled an empirical benchmark over the learners evaluated at every appearance in the Results, Discussion and Conclusions, and the AUPRC reversal is given its prevalence explanation where the comparison is drawn. What remains is almost entirely damage from the 39% cut: six passages where a sentence was overwritten in place rather than replaced, leaving verbatim duplicates in the Methods, the Participant Characteristics paragraph, the parsimony paragraph and the ceiling paragraph, one of which (\".003 in either direction.\") is outright garbled text in the Results. Two substantive items need attention beyond that. The Discussion's coverage argument compares 0.765 to 0.778 across two different oracle estimators, producing exactly the \"one sequence\" reading that Table S15's own note warns against and inflating an approximately 0.002 increment over the best-learner ceiling into a 0.013 gain. And the Results describe the two pandemic cycles as having \"differed little\" when the post-hoc interval admits change of up to 0.05, a claim the Discussion states correctly and the Results should match. None of these threatens a conclusion; all are fixable in one editing pass.

Revision, and the science underneath it is sound. Every number I checked against results/primary2_*.csv reconciles, including Table 2 in full, the fairness table, the parsimony trajectory, the SHAP values, the net-benefit table, the operating characteristics and the 17-versus-14 gain; the outcome is defined identically in both surveys and the design is correctly and repeatedly described as cross-sectional, with no sentence anywhere implying the model forecasts a future state. The deployment claim is properly bounded to triage, and the Discussion explicitly disclaims any outcome benefit that was not tested. The defects that matter are clinical-reading defects rather than analytic ones. Most consequential is that 1/PPV is labelled the number needed to screen in three places in the manuscript and in the Table S2 definition, glossed as "respondents screened per case identified"; the true figures are about 15 and 10 rather than 6.8 and 4.7, and the appendix table refutes its own definition since a fixed 0.85 sensitivity target must give the same number needed to screen for all three model sizes. Second, the largest subgroup disparity in the study, a false-positive rate of 0.68 in Mexican American against 0.36 in non-Hispanic White respondents pre-pandemic, is tabulated in Table S7 but appears nowhere in the text, and the false-positive rate is omitted from the recommended equity-monitoring set for a tool that flags nearly half the population. Third, differential module non-response is described as affecting Asian and Black respondents while the Hispanic categories, including the very subgroup the fairness rule flags, are omitted from both the sentence and Table S8. Alongside these, the 39% cut has left five verbatim duplications and one truncated fragment in the body, one of which asserts that both validation cycles were collected under the 2015-2018 NHANES design, contradicting Part D. All of this is fixable in a revision without any new analysis, since the required numbers are already in the result files.

Revision, and the manuscript file as it stands should not be sent to a journal. The science reconciles: I opened every primary CSV behind a reported number and found no discrepancy that survives inspection. Internal and external AUROC, the +0.006 between-cycle difference and its interval and P value, both recalibration interval regimes, the fairness flags and their -0.056/-0.072/-0.078/+0.074 magnitudes, the full parsimony trajectory including the 0.0002/0.0044 five-versus-six boundary, operating characteristics, net benefit, the 28%/50% food-insecurity decomposition, the 2,199 runs across 117 experiment files, the oracle range 0.764-0.776 and the 0.765 to 0.778 coverage gain all match the authoritative files to the digit, and the 39% cut did not corrupt a single number I could check. The three "not applicable" rows and the one "not specifically addressed" row are honest rather than convenient. The paper trail, however, has not kept up with the cut. Seven TRIPOD+AI rows point at Methods text that now lives in Parts B-D (items 11, 12b, 19, 21, 22, and both intended-user rows 3b and 27b), so a reviewer auditing the checklist against the paper will repeatedly find nothing at the named location; item 19 is the worst, since the manuscript carries no patient-and-public-involvement statement at all. Item 18c compresses the amendment's provenance into "written before analysis", which is precisely the claim the manuscript, Part A and the cover letter all take care not to make. Two pairs of rows contradict each other (1 versus 2 on the abstract, 12d versus 23b on cluster heterogeneity). Independently, condensation left one corrupted Results sentence, four verbatim duplicated sentences, two orphaned paragraphs, and one place where any-item and three-or-more-item non-response rates are presented as if comparable. None of this touches a conclusion; all of it is repairable in one editing pass, after which the checklist should be re-walked row by row against the final text rather than against the pre-cut draft.

Revision, and the revision is mechanical rather than scientific. The science holds together after the 39% cut: I checked every number in the Abstract, Table 2, the parsimony ladder, the sensitivity panel, the fairness panel, the operating point and the net-benefit figures against results/primary2_*.csv and every one reproduces to the digit, including the ones I expected to fail (the 0.823/0.810/0.830 matched-sample-size trio, which is not in 17var_model/results but verifies exactly against results/pathG_02b_kchs_samesize.csv as best-of-three-learners; the 28%/50% food-insecurity share; the -0.056/-0.072/-0.078/+0.074 fairness flags; the 0.0002/0.0044 five-versus-six margin). All five aims are answered in Results, all four hypothesis verdicts are stated and justified, the pronoun and dash bans are clean across the manuscript and Parts A-D, and no cross-reference points at a section the cut removed. What the cut did leave behind is a set of seam defects that a copy editor cannot fix without the authors: four places where a rewritten sentence was inserted without deleting the sentence it replaced (Methods NHANES description, Methods ECE, Results non-response, Results five-versus-six), one corrupted fragment mid-sentence (\".003 in either direction.\"), one promise in Methods that the Results no longer keeps (temperature scaling), one orphan with no antecedent left in the body (\"the stricter-margin seven-item variant\"), one stray sentence stranded outside its paragraph, and two claims that lost the qualifier that made them true (the Abstract's ceiling claim, which its own Tables S11 and S13 contradict on the post-pandemic cohort, and the non-response comparison that silently switches definitions mid-paragraph). The one substantive gap is in Clinical and Policy Implications, where the deployment contrast between the six-item and 17-predictor forms omits that the full model cannot be scored from an individual's answers at all, a point the paper makes in Part D and in Data Availability but not where a reader deciding what to deploy will look. None of these is a reason to reject; all of them are reasons not to send it out in this state.
